program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The edited image does place a mug to the right of the headphones, but it also shows another mug left of them and a conspicuous blurred blue mug-shaped remnant at the source location. Thus the repeated “complete/yes” judgments appear to assess only whether a right-side mug exists, not whether the requested mug was moved and the edit is complete; this conflicts with the partial reference and the rubric’s all-changes-complete criterion. Repair the node’s binding/criteria to track the source mug across source and edited images, distinguish relocation from duplication or residual artifacts, and represent partial progress when the target appears at the destination but remains at or is duplicated from its original location. Keep insufficient visual evidence unresolved rather than inferring completion. The traces are consistently high-confidence and valid, with no dependency or transport failures, so focus on the visual criterion and object correspondence—not confidence or routing.
